questions.stem:
The ratio of mass percentage (w/w) of C : H in a hydrocarbon is 12 : 1. It has two carbon atoms. The weight (in g) of $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$ formed when 3.38 g of this hydrocarbon is completely burnt in oxygen is :
(Given : Molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ C: 12, H: 1, O: 16)
questions.solution:
mass ratio = 12 : 1
mole ratio $= \frac{12}{12} : \frac{1}{1} = 1 : 1$
EF = CH
MF = $\mathrm{C_2H_2}$
$$\mathrm{C_2H_2 + \frac{5}{2}O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + H_2O}$$
mole of $\mathrm{C_2H_2} = \frac{3.38}{26} = 0.13\ \mathrm{mol}$
moles of $\mathrm{CO_2} = 0.13 \times 2 = 0.26$ mol
moles of $\mathrm{CO_2} = 0.26 \times 44 = 11.44$ mol

questions.stem: The first and second ionization constants of a weak dibasic acid $\mathrm{H_2A}$ are $8.1 \times 10^{-8}$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-13}$ respectively. 0.1 mol of $\mathrm{H_2A}$ was dissolved in 1 L of 0.1 M HCl solution. The concentration of $\mathrm{HA^-}$ in the resultant solution is :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{H_2A \rightleftharpoons H^+ + HA^-}$ ; $\mathrm{HCl \rightarrow H^+ + A^-}$
$$K_{a_1} = \frac{[\mathrm{H^+}][\mathrm{HA^-}]}{[\mathrm{H_2A}]}$$
$$8.1 \times 10^{-8} = \frac{(0.1) \times [\mathrm{HA^-}]}{0.1}$$
$$[\mathrm{HA^-}] = 8.1 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{M}$$

questions.stem: Gas 'A' undergoes change from state 'X' to state 'Y'. In this process, the heat absorbed and work done by the gas is 10 J and 18 J respectively. Now gas is brought back to state 'X' by another process during which 6 J of heat is evolved. In the reverse process of 'Y' to 'X',
questions.solution:
$\Delta U = Q + W$
1. Forward Process $(X \rightarrow y)$
$Q_1 = +10\ \mathrm{J}$
$W_1 = -18\ \mathrm{J}$
$\Delta U_{xy} = -8\ \mathrm{J}$
(2) Reverse Process $(y \rightarrow x)$
$\Delta U_{yx} = +8\ \mathrm{J}$
$Q_2 = -6\ \mathrm{J}$
$\Delta U_{yx} = Q_2 + W_2$
$W_2 = +14\ \mathrm{J}$

options.text: 18 J of the work is done by the gas 'A'
2 J of the work is done by the gas 'A'.
12 J of the work is done on the gas 'A' by the surrounding.
14 J of the work is done on the gas 'A' by the surrounding.

questions.stem:
Solution A is prepared by dissolving 1 g of a protein (molar mass = 50000 $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) in 0.5 L of water at 300 K. Its osmotic pressure is $x$ bar. Solution B is made by dissolving 2 g of same protein in 1 L of water at 300 K. Osmotic pressure of solution B is y bar. Entire solution of A is mixed with entire solution of B at same temperature. The osmotic pressure of resultant solution is z bar, x, y and z respectively are :
(R = 0.083 $\mathrm{L\,bar\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
Solution-A
$$\pi = \frac{n}{V}RT = \frac{1}{50000} \times \frac{1}{0.5} \times 0.083 \times 300$$
$x = 9.96 \times 10^{-4}$ bar
Solution-B
$$\pi = \frac{n}{V}RT = \frac{2}{50000} \times \frac{1}{1} \times 0.083 \times 300$$
$y = 9.96 \times 10^{-4}$ bar
Resultant Solution
Total mass = 3 g
Total Volume = 0.5 + 1 = 1.5 L
New Conc$^{n}$. $= \frac{3}{1.5} = 2$
$\pi = CRT = 2 \times 0.083 \times 300$
$Z = 9.96 \times 10^{-4}$ bar

questions.stem:
At $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$, 20.0 mL of 0.2 M weak monoprotic acid HX is titrated against 0.2 M NaOH. The pH of the solution (a) at the start of the titration (when NaOH has not been added) and (b) when 10 mL of NaOH is added respectively, are :
Given : $K_a = 5 \times 10^{-4}$
$\mathrm{p}K_a = 3.3$
$\alpha \ll 1$
questions.solution:
(a) $\alpha \ll 1$
$[\mathrm{H^+}] = \sqrt{K_a \cdot C} = 10^{-2}$
pH = 2.0
(b) m mol of HX = 4
m mol of NaOH = 2
$\mathrm{HX + NaOH \rightarrow NaX + H_2O}$
4 | 2 | 0
2 | 0 | 2
$$\mathrm{pH} = \mathrm{p}K_a + \log_{10}\frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]}$$
pH = 3.3

questions.stem:
Consider the reaction $\mathrm{aX \rightarrow bY}$, for which the rate constant at $30^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is $1 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}\,L\,s^{-1}}$. Which of the following statements are true ?
A. When concentration of 'X' is increased to four times, the rate of reaction becomes 16 times.
B. The reaction is a second order reaction.
C. The half-life period is independent of the concentration of X.
D. Decomposition of $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ is an example of the above reaction.
E. The graph of $\ln\frac{[\mathrm{R_0}]}{[\mathrm{R}]}$ versus time shown in the figure (a straight line through the origin) is valid for the above reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$K = 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{L\,mol^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$
From unit it is second order (n = 2)
Rate $= k[x]^{2}$
if [x] is made 4 times
then rate becomes 16 times
$\rightarrow (t_{1/2})_{n=2} = \frac{1}{K[A]_0}$
$\rightarrow$ Decomposition of $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ is $1^{st}$ order
$\rightarrow \ln\left(\frac{[R_0]}{[R]}\right) = kt$ is for 1st order.

options.text: A, B, D and E only

Statement I: Among Zn, Mn, Sc and Cu, the energy required to remove the third valence electron is highest for Zn and lowest for Sc.
Statement II: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of CFSE is $\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)_6]^{2+} < [Co(H_2O)_6]^{3+} < [Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Element | $\mathrm{IE_3}$ (kJ/mol)
Sc | 2393
Mn | 3260
Cu | 3556
Zn | 3837
$\mathrm{IE_3}$ : Sc < Mn < Cu < Zn
$\rightarrow$ on moving from left to right $Z_{\text{eff}}$ increases $\Rightarrow$ IE increases
$\rightarrow$ CFSE $\propto$ oxidation state of metal
CFSE $\propto$ strength of ligand
$\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)_6]^{2+} < [Co(H_2O)_6]^{3+} < [Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$

If the % of carbon is 25% and of hydrogen is 4.89%, then X = ____ $\times 10^{-3}$ g. (Nearest integer) (Molar mass of C, H and O are 12, 1 and 16 $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively.)
questions.solution:

$25 = \frac{12}{44} \times \frac{25}{\text{wt. of OC}}$
wt. of OC = 0.02726

questions.stem:
Correct statements regarding alkyl halides (R - X) among the following are :
A. Alcohol being less polar solvent as compared to water, alcoholic KOH favours elimination reaction with R – X.
B. Order of reactivity towards $\mathrm{S_N1}$ mechanism is $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}CH_2{-}Cl > C_6H_5{-}CHCl{-}C_6H_5}$.
C. Non substituted aryl halides exhibit properties similar to alkyl halides.
D. Vinyl chloride is an example of haloalkene and allyl chloride is an example of haloalkyne.
E. R – Cl can be prepared by reacting R – OH with $\mathrm{SOCl_2}$ but Ar-Cl cannot be prepared by reacting Ar-OH with $\mathrm{SOCl_2}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{R{-}X \xrightarrow{aq.\ KOH}}$ Nucleophilic substitution
$\mathrm{R{-}X \xrightarrow{Alc.\ KOH}}$ Elimination
$\mathrm{S_N1} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ph{-}\overset{\oplus}{C}H_2 < Ph{-}\overset{\oplus}{C}H{-}Ph}$
Vinyl Chloride $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}Cl}$ (Haloalkene)
Allyl Chloride $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH_2{-}Cl}$ (not haloalkyne)
$\mathrm{R{-}OH \xrightarrow[S_Ni]{SOCl_2} R{-}Cl}$
$\mathrm{Ph{-}OH \xrightarrow{SOCl_2}} \times$
Phenol do not give $\mathrm{S_Ni}$ reaction with $\mathrm{SOCl_2}$ due to partial double bond character in C–O bond.

questions.stem:
The surface of sodium metal is irradiated with radiation of wavelength x nm. The kinetic energy of ejected electrons is $2.8 \times 10^{-20}$ J. The work function of sodium is 2.3 eV. The value of x is ________ $\times 10^{2}$ nm. (Nearest integer)
(Given : $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$; $1\ \mathrm{eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$; $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
$E - E^\circ = KE$ — (1)
$E^\circ = 2.3 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J} = 3.68 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$
$KE = 0.28 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$
using (1), $E = 3.96 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$
$\lambda = \frac{hc}{E} = 500\ \mathrm{nm}$
$= 5 \times 10^{2}$ nm

Consider the following gas phase reaction being carried out in a closed vessel at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

time (min) | total pressure of the system (mm Hg)
30 | 300
$\infty$ | 600
The pressure of C(g) at 30 minutes time interval would be ________ mm Hg. (nearest integer)

Consider the following two half-cell reactions along with the standard reduction potential given :
$\mathrm{CO_2 + 6H^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow CH_3OH + H_2O}$ ; $E^\circ_{\text{red}} = 0.02\ \mathrm{V}$
$\mathrm{\frac{1}{2}O_2 + 2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow H_2O}$ ; $E^\circ_{\text{red}} = 1.23\ \mathrm{V}$
A fuel cell was set up using the above two reactions such that the cell operates under the standard condition of 1 bar pressure and 298 K temperature. The fuel cell works with 80 % efficiency. If the work derived from the cell using 1 mol of $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$ is used to compress an ideal gas isothermally against a constant pressure of 1 kPa, then the change in the volume of the gas, $\Delta V$ = ________ $\mathrm{m^3}$. (nearest integer)
Given: F = 96500 $\mathrm{C\,mol^{-1}}$
questions.solution:
Anode : $\mathrm{CH_3OH + H_2O \rightarrow CO_2 + 6H^+ + 5e^-}$
Cathode : $\mathrm{\frac{1}{2}O_2 + 2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow H_2O}$
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_C - E^\circ_A = 1.23 - 0.02 = 1.21\ \mathrm{V}$
$|W_{\max}| = |\Delta G| = nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}}$
$= 6 \times 96500 \times 1.21 = 700590\ \mathrm{J}$
$W_{\text{act}} = 0.8 \times 700590 = 560472\ \mathrm{J}$
$W_{\text{act}} = |P_{\text{ext}}\Delta V|$
$P_{\text{ext}} = 1000$ Pascal
$560472 = 1000 \times |\Delta V|$
$\Delta V = 560.472\ \mathrm{m^3} \approx 560$
